papers.title_in_file: Attendee Guide: A Self-Paced Quantum Learning Journey (Quantum Explorers, July 2023 - February 2024)
papers.what_it_is: IBM's attendee guide to its Quantum Explorers beginner program (July 2023 to February 2024): badges, timeline, credentials, Discord and Jupyter usage, and FAQ; a program logistics document with no technical results.

assertions.value: The guide describes Quantum Explorers as a self-paced, game-based quantum computing learning program for high school students and above, and as a beginner-level program.
assertions.anchor: About the Quantum Explorers Program, p.3
quotes: Quantum Explorers is a self-paced, gamebased quantum computing learning program for high school students and above.
This is a beginner-level program for people interested in quantum computing.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints 'gamebased'; the value reads it as 'game-based'.

assertions.value: The guide gives the program period as July 2023 to February 2024, and says Discord goes to read-only mode in February.
assertions.anchor: Cover page and Timeline, p.1 and p.6
quotes: JULY 2023 - FEBRUARY 2024
DISCORD ON READ-ONLY MODE
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide's own statement of the program's scope in time.
assertions.reader_inference: The timeline graphic is flattened in the text layer, so the pairing of 'read-only mode' with February rests on the layout order and the cover dates.

assertions.value: The guide states that there are seven themed achievements to unlock, with corresponding badges to collect, in two categories: learning badges and community badges.
assertions.anchor: About the Quantum Explorers Program, p.3; About Achievements, p.4
quotes: There are seven themed achievements to unlock, with corresponding badges to collect.
There are two types of space exploration themed badge achievements: learning and community.
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide defines its own achievement structure.

assertions.value: The guide states that Explorers will gain a high-level understanding of quantum computing and some of its applications, and will program real quantum computers.
assertions.anchor: About the Quantum Explorers Program, p.3
quotes: Participants (Explorers) will gain a high-level understanding of quantum computing, some of its applications, and
program real quantum computers.
assertions.certainty_reason: A stated outcome with no evidence of learner results in the guide.
assertions.reader_inference: The two quotes are consecutive lines of one sentence; the text layer breaks the sentence across a column break.

assertions.value: The guide lists seven badges with these topics: Captain (Quantum Computing & Qiskit 101), Time Traveler (Quantum Error Correction & Mitigation), Space Combatant (Quantum Machine Learning), Expert Navigator (Quantum Optimization), Eminent Scientist (Quantum Women Invited Talks), Prime Ambassador (Discord Activity & Community Events) and Supreme Observer (IBM Quantum Challenge Fall 2023).
quotes: Quantum Computing & Qiskit 101 #q-computing-101
Quantum Error Correction & Mitigation #q-error-cm
Quantum Machine Learning #q-machine-learning
Quantum Optimization #q-optimization
Quantum Women Invited Talks #q-women-invited-talks
Discord Activity & Community Events #q-prime-ambassador
IBM Quantum Challenge Fall 2023 #ibmq-challenge
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide's own statement of the program's topics.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer lists badge names and topics as two separate runs; the name-to-topic pairing follows list order, and the one-to-one pairing is the reader's reading of the flattened layout. The KEY (learning versus community) colors are not in the text, so which badge is which type is not stated in the extracted text.

assertions.value: The guide states that total materials cover approximately 50 to 85 hours and that the level of engagement depends on the participant.
quotes: Total materials cover approximately 50 to 85 hours.
Level of engagement depends on you.
assertions.certainty_reason: IBM's estimate of its own program's workload.

assertions.value: The guide states that only the Captain badge is available at program launch, and that dates and times may change during the program, with the #announcements channel the best source of updates.
quotes: Only the Captain badge will be available at program launch.
Dates and times may be subject to change throughout the course of the program.
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide's own stated limit on the timeline.

assertions.value: The guide names these events in its timeline: the Global Quantum Game Jam and the Quantum Explorers Quantum Creative Winter Fest.
quotes: EVENT: GLOBAL QUANTUM GAME JAM
EVENT: QUANTUM EXPLORERS QUANTUM CREATIVE WINTER
assertions.certainty_reason: Event names from a flattened graphic; their dates are not in the text layer.
assertions.reader_inference: The second event name continues on the next line of the text layer ('FEST'); the name is read as 'Quantum Explorers Quantum Creative Winter Fest'.

assertions.value: The guide states that each learning badge has a quiz assessment in its jupyter notebook that must be passed with a score of at least 80 percent, and that a password is revealed on successful completion.
assertions.anchor: How to Unlock a Badge Achievement, Step 3, p.7
quotes: Each learning badge has a quiz assessment in its jupyter notebook that you must pass by achieving a score percentage of at least 80%.
A password will be revealed on successful completion.
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide's own statement of its assessment rule.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says 'score percentage of at least 80%'; the paper does not describe the quiz questions, so the assessment's difficulty is not stated.

assertions.value: The guide states that each community badge has a single question that assesses a string password provided when the participant is eligible, and that passwords must not be shared because they prove an achievement was unlocked.
assertions.anchor: How to Unlock a Badge Achievement, Step 3, p.7
quotes: Each community badge has a single question that assesses a string password that you will be provided when you are eligible to unlock the badge.
Do NOT share the passwords with anyone!
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide's own statement of its verification rule.

assertions.value: The guide states that admins verify an achievement after the participant shares progress in the #level-up channel, and that this can take up to five working days.
assertions.anchor: How to Unlock a Badge Achievement, Step 4, p.8
quotes: Please allow up to five working days for admins to verify your achievement and add the Discord label to your name.
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide's own statement of its verification process.

assertions.value: The guide states the eligibility criteria for IBM digital credentials issued via Credly: Participant needs 1/3 community achievements, Foundational needs 1/4 learning achievements, Intermediate needs 4/4 learning achievements, and Advanced needs 7/7 total achievements.
quotes: Participant - 1/3 community achievements
Foundational - 1/4 learning achievements
Intermediate - 4/4 learning achievements
Advanced - 7/7 total achievements
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide defines its own credential criteria.
assertions.reader_inference: The text writes the criteria as '1/3' and '1/4'; read with 'Advanced - 7/7', these appear to mean at least one of three community badges and at least one of four learning badges, but the guide does not spell out that reading. Counts also imply four learning and three community badges, which the guide's badge list does not mark in the text layer.

assertions.value: The guide states in its FAQ that a participant must achieve the rank of Captain before starting the other learning module badges, and states in the Discord section that unlocking Captain opens the rest of the server and more channels.
assertions.anchor: FAQ, p.18; How to Navigate Discord, Helpful Channels and Roles, p.13
quotes: You’ll need to achieve the rank of Captain before being able to start the other learning module Badges.
Once you unlock the rank of Captain, the rest of the server and more channels will be available to you.
assertions.reader_inference: Page 7 says participants may choose any order of badges and that Captain first is encouraged, and the FAQ on p.18 says only Captain is required first. The guide is internally consistent on the exception for Captain.

assertions.value: The guide states that to enter the Discord server a participant must confirm registration for the 2023-24 cohort and being above the age of 14.
assertions.anchor: How to Navigate Discord, Step 2, p.10
quotes: asks if you have registered for the 2023-24 cohort of Quantum Explorers and are above the age of 14.
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide's own stated entry condition.
assertions.reader_inference: The program is described as for 'high school students and above' on p.3; the guide gives no reconciliation of that audience with the age-14 confirmation.

assertions.value: The guide states that the lab exercises are jupyter notebooks that run in the IBM Quantum Lab, a cloud-based jupyter notebook environment, and that notebooks from the Quantum Explorers GitHub repository are downloaded and uploaded to the Lab after logging in to an IBM Quantum Platform account.
assertions.anchor: Using Jupyter Notebooks in the Cloud, p.14 and p.15
quotes: These can be run in the IBM Quantum Lab, which is a cloud-based jupyter notebook environment.
Once you’ve logged into your IBM Quantum Platform account, go to the Lab.

assertions.value: The guide states that Qiskit is an open source Python framework used to program quantum computers, and that it can be used locally after installing it or in the cloud through the Lab on IBM Quantum Platform.
quotes: Qiskit is an open source Python framework used to program quantum computers.
or you can use it in the cloud without installing it by accessing the Lab on IBM Quantum Platform.

assertions.value: The guide states that all lectures and invited talks will be recorded and available for the duration of the program, that live social events will not be recorded, and that participants may not publicly share most program materials (workbooks, guidebooks, live event recordings, Discord screenshots) but may post their unlocked badge images.
quotes: All lectures and invited talks will be recorded and available for viewing at any time for the duration of the Quantum Explorers program.
Live social events will not be recorded
You cannot upload and publicly share our learning materials like the workbooks, guidebooks, live event recordings, screenshots of our Discord server, etc.
assertions.certainty_reason: The guide's own stated terms of use.
assertions.reader_inference: The guide's material is restricted to registered attendees, so the technical content of the program (including the Quantum Machine Learning module) is not in this document and cannot be checked from it.

assertions.value: The guide states that top performing Explorers will be highlighted at the end of the program.
assertions.anchor: About the Quantum Explorers Program, p.3
quotes: Top performing Explorers will be highlighted at the end of the program.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement of intent; the guide gives no ranking criterion.
